title: Redis-backed caching for slow backend reads, starting with Friends overview
spec: Switching from Profile to Friends (and likely other reads) is slow every time -- there is currently zero caching on backend read endpoints. friends_overview (backend/users/friends.py) runs three uncached DB queries on every call. The infrastructure for Redis already exists and is unused for this: backend/backend/settings.py wires Django CACHES with a three-tier fallback (Redis via REDIS_URL, else shared DatabaseCache, else local LocMemCache), redis is already in requirements.txt, and backend/users/leaderboard.py has its own separate direct-redis-client pattern for sorted-set ranking only. Task: 1) Research and pick the best-fit managed Redis provider for this stack (Vercel serverless Django + Supabase Postgres already using a transaction pooler due to IPv6/connection issues, see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) -- weigh HTTP/REST-based options that avoid persistent-connection problems in serverless, not just the cheapest choice. Document exact setup steps (account, env var names, region) in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md but do NOT create the account or spend money -- the owner adds real credentials afterward. 2) Using the existing Django CACHES abstraction (not the leaderboard raw-client pattern), add caching to friends_overview and audit other slow, frequently-repeated reads across trivia/ and users/ for the same treatment, with correct invalidation (e.g. friends_overview must invalidate immediately on a friend/request/block action for the affected users, not just time out). 3) Must work correctly with zero Redis configured today (falls back to DatabaseCache). This is an infrastructure-level, multi-endpoint change -- treat as needing a real design pass, not a single-file patch.

title: Cut the post-game score reveal delay
spec: The post-game reveal takes too long. In GameResult.tsx the score is already a known number the instant a game ends (games already track points as the player answers) -- nothing is actually being calculated when the Calculating score... loader shows. In MiniGame.tsx around the showResult effect, the flow is: hide the result, await a POST to /trivia/log-session/ to award points, THEN wait an unconditional setTimeout of 1500ms, THEN reveal. That fixed 1.5s pause is pure dead time with no real work behind it. Fix: show the result immediately (or with a short, under 300ms, polish transition) without gating on the point-award request finishing -- let awardPoints keep running in the background and dispatch the awarded points to redux whenever its response lands, independent of when the reveal animation plays. Keep the existing AnimatedNumber count-up and confetti, they are already fine; only remove the extra artificial wait. Verify in a real browser across at least two different games (e.g. wordle and one non-daily game) that the result appears promptly, points still get awarded correctly, and a slow or failed log-session call does not block or break the reveal.

title: Confirm and extend robots.txt (sitemap reference, AI-crawler stance)
spec: Current public/robots.txt is minimal: User-agent star, Allow /, Disallow /admin, no Sitemap line. Research findings: Google/RFC 9309 recognize only User-agent, Allow, Disallow, Sitemap; groups do not inherit from the star group, so any dedicated bot group must repeat Disallow /admin itself; Sitemap must be an absolute URL and can be listed even before the sitemap.xml task ships (use the real production domain); Crawl-delay is ignored by Google (recommend omitting); never disallow /_next or any JS/CSS path since this is a client-rendered app and blocking those breaks indexing of rendered content; Disallow is not the same as noindex, a disallowed page can still appear index-only, so keep the existing page-level noindex on /admin as-is rather than relying on robots.txt alone. AI crawlers split into three classes: training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, meta-externalagent, Bytespider), search/answer-engine crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Googlebot, Bingbot), and user-triggered fetchers. For a free discoverability-driven trivia site with no proprietary content to protect, the recommendation is to stay fully permissive (allow all of the above) rather than block training bots, since blocking has no upside here and could reduce visibility in AI answer engines. Task: keep the current Allow-all-except-admin shape, add a Sitemap line once the production domain is known (coordinate with the sitemap.xml work in the SEO card), and do not add crawl-delay, host or noindex lines. Separately flag, do not fix here: /coming-soon currently returns HTTP 200 with not-found content, a soft 404, which should get a real notFound() or noindex fix in a future task.

expected.note: one config line

title: Rewrite stale llms.txt to match the current live game list
spec: Current public/llms.txt is stale: it lists hidden/removed games (connections, heatmap, stat grids) and wrongly calls the app a single-page React application (it is Next.js SSR/App Router). Research findings (llms.txt v2 spec, llmstxt.org, Aug 2026): required structure is one H1 site name, a one-paragraph blockquote summary, optional plain paragraphs, then ## sections each a Markdown link list (Title, url, one-line note). Content rules: 10-30 curated links grouped by product surface not site hierarchy, absolute https URLs, a Last reviewed date line, no marketing fluff, no tech-stack trivia, no auth-gated or hidden-feature links. Honest caveat backed by traffic data (Google explicitly says it is not used for Search; measured AI-agent logs show well under 1 percent of sites get any llms.txt fetches at all): treat this as cheap hygiene, not an SEO lever, but a stale file that misinforms agents is worse than none. Task: rewrite public/llms.txt to list exactly the current visibleGames from src/utils/GameUtils.tsx (10 games today, do not hardcode a count that will drift), remove every hidden game and the /admin mention, add a short accounts/leaderboard/multiplayer section, and a Last reviewed date. Keep it under about 40 lines. Bonus if time allows: add app/llms.txt/route.ts generated from visibleGames so this cannot go stale again, and a small <link rel=describedby href=/llms.txt type=text/markdown> tag in the root layout per the v2 discovery convention.
